A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MoNE, with matching core methods and retained experiments. All 19 pages of v1 and 27 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original pruning experiments, nine-task accuracy results, component ablations, continued pretraining and inference measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds larger-model evaluations, Math/GSM8K experiments, scoring ablations and revised inference measurements.

M1.justification: The frequency–variance product, expert selection, mean-output novices and routing-based inference remain unchanged. Alternative scoring formulations are tested as ablations rather than adopted as a revised method. Equation 8's mathematical revision is assessed under T1.

E1.justification: Appendix A adds actual evaluations on Math and GSM8K, including calibration using their training data. This substantially extends task coverage beyond the retained nine general-language benchmarks. Zyda2, C4 and OLMoE-mix-0924 remain in use.

E2.justification: Angular, FLAP, MC-SMoE and RS remain the accuracy baselines. However, v1's latency comparison against all four methods is removed; v2 Table 16 compares pruned MoNE models only with the unpruned model. Newly cited MoE-Pruner and SlimMoE are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds Qwen2-57B-A14B, Qwen3-30B-A3B and instruct/chat configurations, an accuracy-constrained maximum-pruning evaluation, and calibration using the first 100 specialized-task training samples. The latency protocol changes from three models using HuggingFace and downstream prompts to Qwen3 using SGLang, fixed 512-token inputs and 256-token outputs, and batch sizes 1, 128 and 512.

E4.justification: Figure 4 expands component ablations from three to five conditions, adding frequency-only and variance-only pruning without novices. Appendix B adds normalized, log-sum and three weighted scoring variants. Specialized-task calibration comparisons and batch-size/novice-hit analyses substantially expand investigation of sensitivity and failure conditions.

E5.justification: v2 Table 16 newly reports input-generation seeds 1020 and 1998 with separate measurements. This documents input variation, not an increase in replicated accuracy runs. The condition-wise standard deviations in Figure 3 remain unchanged; neither version adds confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: The original three-model accuracy tables, five supplementary calibration tables and continued-pretraining scores are retained numerically. Substantial new results cover Qwen models, pruning limits, specialized tasks and scoring variants. For example, new Qwen3 results at 50% pruning show RS at 68.06 versus MoNE at 66.32 (Table 10). Latency results are replaced under different conditions, not improved under a matched protocol.

T1.justification: Equation 8 changes from the norm of summed residuals to the sum of individual residual norms, a substantive local mathematical revision. The claimed mean-output solution remains, although the revised unsquared-norm objective does not generally justify it. Appendix B also adds an argument about log-sum/product ranking equivalence.

C1.justification: The core novice-based compression and robustness claims persist. The abstract and contribution list replace the highlighted 50% pruning advantage with a claim of only 0.14 accuracy-point loss for Qwen2 at 25% pruning, while correcting the highlighted 25% baseline advantage from 2.71 to 2.72.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations concerning larger-model redundancy, specialized-task calibration mismatch, model-dependent scoring sensitivity, and latency dependence on batch size and novice hits. The standalone limitations section disappears: its 16B-only evaluation limitation is addressed, while its discussion of combining pruning methods is omitted. New applicability qualifications instead appear throughout the evaluation and appendices.

D1.justification: v2 documents the SGLang transformers backend, built-in profiling utilities and specialized calibration sample selection. Existing continued-pretraining hyperparameters are retained and moved to Section 5.5. Direct checkpoint URLs for the original three models are removed, while the code, evaluation-harness and pretraining-data links remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds references and discussion concerning MoE-Pruner, SlimMoE, task-specific pruning, Qwen models and GPU inference, while removing the Sarathi-Serve reference. These extend the context without substantially redefining MoNE's positioning within structured expert pruning.

P1.justification: Most method prose and the main narrative remain intact. Targeted edits revise the abstract and conclusion, relocate pretraining details, reorganize appendices and add an appendix roadmap. Author notes are updated, and actual acknowledgments replace v1's template instructions.

P2.justification: The main accuracy table is expanded and split by pruning ratio; new tables present specialized tasks, scoring variants and pruning limits. Ablation plots gain rows, the latency chart is replaced by a table, and appendix tables and heatmaps are substantially rearranged under a different document style. v2 Figure 13 also incorrectly labels all three model panels DeepSeek-V2-Lite.

improvement.justification: The larger-model evaluations address v1's explicit 16B-only limitation, while expanded ablations and specialized-task calibration tests better establish applicability and failure conditions. These gains are tempered by the loss of comparative efficiency evidence, retained outperformance claims contradicted by new Qwen results, the problematic Equation 8 revision and Figure 13's model-label errors.
